headline: A one-year law lets states move some clean water loan funds into drinking water loan funds to address lead exposure threats.
what_it_does: For one year, a state may shift up to 5% of the total federal grant money it has received for its clean water state revolving fund into its drinking water state revolving fund. The transfer is allowed only to address a public health threat from heightened lead exposure in drinking water. The title also says the bill includes other provisions, but the official summary describes only this transfer authority.

who_it_affects.group: State governments that run clean water and drinking water state revolving funds
who_it_affects.how: They gain temporary authority to move up to 5% of their clean water fund's cumulative federal grant amount into their drinking water fund to respond to lead risks.

who_it_affects.group: Residents served by public drinking water systems in areas with lead exposure concerns
who_it_affects.how: Their state may use the transferred money to help fund drinking water work aimed at reducing lead exposure.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 4, 2019; the transfer authority lasts for one year.
